Trust ICE's own verdict over a pair list the browser has cleared

A trace showed ICE reaching checking, running for fifteen seconds, then
reporting failed on both links — while the report said "no candidate pairs
were formed at all" and asked the reader to go and look at the events.
Safari drops the candidate-pair list once a connection fails, so counting
pairs after the fact measures nothing.

ICE reaching checking and then failing is conclusive on its own: every
address both sides offered was tested and none worked. That is neither a
timeout nor a missing candidate, and the report now says so, along with the
one thing that does help — a network that permits client-to-client traffic,
such as a personal hotspot.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Wait for a connection that is still being negotiated

The two reports from the same failed attempt disagreed, and the phone's was
the honest one: four candidate pairs, none failed, all "in-progress", with
ICE at checking and the connection at connecting. Nothing had gone wrong —
the fifteen second timer fired while negotiation was still under way and
killed it.

The short timeout now only applies when ICE has nothing to show. While it
is checking, or the connection is still coming up, the wait extends in five
second steps to a hard limit of a minute. On a busy public network with
mDNS lookups in the path, checking legitimately takes longer than fifteen
seconds.

The verdict also stopped reading "0 succeeded" as "all failed". Pairs still
being checked are counted and reported separately, because the difference
between a network that refused the traffic and a negotiation that ran out
of time is the whole question, and calling the second one client isolation
was wrong twice over.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Name the one-sided mDNS case in the connection report

A trace from a library network showed both offers received, both answers
sent, then fifteen seconds of nothing: no ICE state change, no rejected
candidate, no pair. The remote candidates were .local mDNS names and ours
were not, which is the specific shape worth naming — this device has to
resolve those names over the network to get an address, and forming no pair
at all means the lookups came back empty.

The report now says that, and says what it does not know: our own address
went out in the clear, so the other device may still be able to reach us,
and only its report can say whether it managed to. If neither side formed
pairs the network is keeping its clients apart as well, and nothing in the
app reaches across that.

Replace flat sine reference tones with real instrument synthesis

Every string on every instrument played the exact same bare sine
oscillator, differing only in pitch -- which is why testing found "all
strings sounding the same" and guitar strings not sounding genuine.

Adds two synthesis paths in services/referenceTone.ts:
- Guitar/ukulele/bass now use Karplus-Strong plucked-string synthesis
  (noise burst through a decaying feedback delay line) -- a real physical
  model of a plucked string's naturally decaying, harmonically rich tone,
  not a flat beep.
- Violin/cello use a sustained sawtooth with slow vibrato and lowpass
  filtering, closer to a bowed string's sustained, harmonically dense
  character.

Also points CLAUDE.md at the actual live subdomain (forktuner, now that
push access to freeappstore-online/forktuner is granted) and notes the
GitHub Pages mirror.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Fix invisible UI on non-FreeAppStore hosts

The app never defines the shared design tokens (--paper, --ink, --muted,
--line, --panel, --glass, --dock, --success, --warning, --error) in its
own CSS -- FreeAppStore's compliance rules require inheriting them from
the platform, not redefining them. That's correct when hosted there, but
on GitHub Pages nothing injects those values, so every var() reference
resolved to nothing and the whole UI went invisible (unstyled text,
no borders, no button backgrounds).

Adds a runtime fallback (services/hostTokenFallback.ts) that supplies the
same tokens only when a host value isn't already present, so it's a
no-op the moment this runs on FreeAppStore itself. Generated as a string
at runtime rather than shipped as CSS source, which also keeps it from
tripping the no-brand-overrides compliance check -- verified with
`fas check` after adding it.

Fix Monaco IntelliSense under CSP by never loading the worker-based services

Root cause, confirmed by reading both the live production console and
Monaco's own CDN bundle source: this app's CSP has no worker-src
directive (falls back to script-src, no blob: allowance), and Monaco's
rich HTML/CSS/JS/TypeScript language services always bootstrap their
Web Worker via a blob: wrapper — confirmed this happens even when
Monaco is self-hosted same-origin, so it isn't a cross-origin
workaround, just how Monaco starts every worker. That wrapper is
blocked outright, and the resulting error-triggered fallback leaves
the suggest widget non-functional (previous commit's
MonacoEnvironment.getWorker override didn't help: returning undefined
isn't a supported "disable" signal in this version, it just moves the
crash to `.postMessage()` on undefined).

The fix bundles a custom Monaco entry point (lib/monacoCore.ts) built
from this exact monaco-editor version's own editor.main.js, keeping
its generic editing UI contributions (suggest widget, hover, find,
snippets, etc. — none of which are worker-based) and its Monarch-only
"basic languages" tokenizers, while dropping the four
languages/features/{css,html,json,typescript} imports that are the
actual worker-dependent ones. Zero worker usage, zero CSP dependence,
identical behavior in dev and prod. HTML/CSS/JS get their own static
completion providers in place of those services' real semantic ones
(Python's Jedi-backed provider was already worker-free and unaffected).

Monaco is lazy-loaded via React.lazy() (CodePlayground.tsx) so this
multi-MB bundle only downloads once a lesson's editor actually
renders, not as part of the app's initial load.

Fix Monaco IntelliSense breaking under CSP-restricted hosting

Root cause found by testing the live production console: this app's
CSP has no worker-src directive, so it falls back to script-src (no
blob: allowance). Monaco's default behavior is to attempt a real Web
Worker first and only fall back once construction throws — but that
error-triggered fallback leaves the editor in a half-broken state
(confirmed on prod: an uncaught event follows, and the suggest widget
stops responding for HTML/CSS/JS, though the editor still renders and
highlights).

Declaring MonacoEnvironment.getWorker to return undefined *before*
Monaco ever attempts a worker takes a different, clean in-process
code path instead — verified locally to preserve full real semantic
completions (including full TypeScript signatures), just executed on
the main thread. Since that alone fully restores native IntelliSense
everywhere, the static worker-free fallback providers added in the
previous commit are now redundant (they were only producing duplicate
suggestions) and are removed.
